channel.title: Israel National News Flashes
channel.description: Latest news flashes from Israel National News

item.title: Bennett open to haredi parties, demands 'advancing the revolution for those who serve'
item.description: 'Together' party leader Naftali Bennett welcomes Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's willingness to form a unity government based on 'alliance of those who serve,' demands state inquiry, prime ministerial term limits.

item.title: Netanyahu's unity government offer met with mixed messages
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's proposal to form a unity government with Gadi Eisenkot, with Eisenkot serving as prime minister first in a rotation agreement, drew a mix of support and skepticism from politicians across the political spectrum.

item.title: Cliff collapses in Herzliya: 'A ticking time bomb'
item.description: A section of the coastal sandstone cliff at Apollonia National Park in Herzliya collapsed Saturday morning, the municipality said. The collapse occurred in an area under the responsibility of the Israel Nature and Parks Authority.

item.title: Meat, eggs and longevity: The Israeli study
item.description: A study following 1,360 women in Israel for about 15 years examines links between meat, egg, and dairy consumption, and mortality risk. Researchers also highlight the role of kosher dietary laws and the importance of participants' ages.

item.title: Soldiers report stone-throwing ambush in Hebron region
item.description: A Palestinian was wounded by gunfire in a-Tuwani in the South Hebron Hills. Honenu says the soldiers who opened fire were attacked with stones and feared for their lives.

item.title: Report: Man breaks into Rabbi Dov Lando's home carrying dangerous object
item.description: Suspect who broke into home of 96-year-old Degel HaTorah leader conveyed threatening messages to him amid talks on forming an alternative government with haredi participation.

item.title: 1146 days of asking the BBC to listen. Now it has to answer
item.description: My bet is that Mann’s report will be damning. Opinion.

item.title: Security forces intercept balloons carrying rifles and drugs
item.description: IDF, Yamas forces intercept balloons carrying weapons and drugs across Israel’s western border, following detection of pistols near eastern border a day earlier.

item.title: The Demographic Revolution: When Islam Overtakes Christianity
item.description: A demographic forecast cited in this column projects that Muslims will outnumber Christians worldwide as early as 2035. L

item.title: "With Laban I sojourned"
item.description: Biblical commentators explain their views on what Yaakov meant with his charge, and more generally in his choice of words.

item.title: Israeli businesswoman arrested in Thailand
item.description: Thai immigration police arrest Hila Suissa at Koh Samui airport on warrant issued in August, after investigating business network linked to Israelis as part of enforcement operation.

item.title: Political drama: Netanyahu agrees to serve second in premiership rotation
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announces willingness to let Gadi Eisenkot serve first in a premiership rotation, calls for immediate negotiations to form unity government.

item.title: Australia names alleged organizers of antisemitic attacks
item.description: Two Australian citizens living in Iran and Iraq were confirmed to be behind a series of attacks on Jewish institutions in Melbourne and Sydney.

item.title: Turkey Is closing six university units in Syria. Why is it planning one in Damascus?
item.description: Turkey has become one of Damascus's most consequential external partners, offering political, economic, educational and security cooperation as the new authorities attempt to consolidate control. Will Turkey soon call the shots or is it being more subtle? Opinion

item.title: Hackers reportedly breach US Air Force cloud platform
item.description: Reported Cloud One intrusion prompted software restrictions and a Cyber Command assessment, attackers’ identity and whether data was stolen remain unknown.

item.title: Mansour Abbas to demand ministerial posts
item.description: Ra'am chairman Mansour Abbas expected to demand ministerial posts for himself and his No. 2, Yoav Segalovitz.

item.title: After losing loved ones, Nir Oz families fight to save homes left standing after massacre
item.description: Kibbutz Nir Oz to demolish homes damaged in the October 7 massacre, bereaved families promise to fight the demolition. Yarden Bibas: 'I don't want to lose the place where we were a family, too.'

item.title: Report warns Russian sabotage in Europe could cause mass casualties
item.description: International Institute for Strategic Studies report finds 16% rise in Russian sabotage in Europe and twice the use of arson and explosives. Researchers warn of a mass-casualty incident and question the efficacy of measures to deter the Kremlin.

item.title: Two terrorists identified as Doctors Without Borders employees
item.description: Two terrorists eliminated in Gaza City were also employed as security guards by the international humanitarian organization Doctors Without Borders (MSF).

item.title: Electric company workers attacked in Binyamin
item.description: Four employees of the Jerusalem District Electricity Company, two of them Israelis, attacked while repairing an electricity pole in Arab village.

item.title: Shabbat Shalom!
item.description:
Arutz Sheva-Israel National News is stopping its round-the-clock news updates at this time in honor of the start of Shabbat in North America, where they are being written now.
Updates will resume Saturday night from Israel, following the conclusion of Shabbat at 17:14 Jerusalem time.
Shabbat Shalom!

item.title: Costa Rica bars anti-Israel UN rapporteur Francesca Albanese from entering country
item.description:
Costa Rica denies entry to anti-Israel UN rapporteur Francesca Albanese, citing an international alert over alleged links to terrorist acts. Israel welcomes move.
(Arutz Sheva-Israel National News' North American desk is keeping you updated until the start of Shabbat in New York. The time posted automatically on all Israel National News articles, however, is Israeli time.)

item.title: Iran threatens action in air and at sea as it vows to break US blockade
item.description:
Senior Iranian officials threaten military action and vow to break the US naval blockade while ruling out the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.
(Arutz Sheva-Israel National News' North American desk is keeping you updated until the start of Shabbat in New York. The time posted automatically on all Israel National News articles, however, is Israeli time.)

item.title: Countdown to Hamas disarmament: Timetable for Gaza demilitarization revealed
item.description:
Israel is expected to approve the Gaza demilitarization plan within days, with a multinational force scheduled to enter the Strip in early 2027.
(Arutz Sheva-Israel National News' North American desk is keeping you updated until the start of Shabbat in New York. The time posted automatically on all Israel National News articles, however, is Israeli time.)

item.title: Watch: US military disables cargo ship attempting to breach naval blockade on Iran
item.description:
CENTCOM announces that US forces disabled a commercial vessel in the Gulf of Oman after it departed an Iranian port and defied repeated blockade warnings.
(Arutz Sheva-Israel National News' North American desk is keeping you updated until the start of Shabbat in New York. The time posted automatically on all Israel National News articles, however, is Israeli time.)

item.title: Bennett: Unity government is preferable, but we are prepared for an alternative
item.description:
Naftali Bennett reiterates his preference for a Zionist unity government led initially by Eisenkot, but says he is prepared to accept an alternative.
(Arutz Sheva-Israel National News' North American desk is keeping you updated until the start of Shabbat in New York. The time posted automatically on all Israel National News articles, however, is Israeli time.)

item.title: Eisenkot vows to form government within eight days, accuses Likud of stalling
item.description:
Gadi Eisenkot vows to form a government before his mandate expires, accusing Likud of stalling. Likud insists it remains committed to a unity government.
(Arutz Sheva-Israel National News' North American desk is keeping you updated until the start of Shabbat in New York. The time posted automatically on all Israel National News articles, however, is Israeli time.)

item.title: Shabbat Shalom from Israel!
item.description:
Arutz Sheva-Israel National News' Israel desk is stopping its round-the-clock news updates at this time in honor of Shabbat. Jerusalem candle lighting time is 15:56 on Friday. Our North American desk will keep you informed until the 16:12 EST candle lighting time in New York.
The updates from Israel will resume Saturday night, following the conclusion of Shabbat at 17:14 in Jerusalem.
Shabbat Shalom!

item.title: Israel’s home prices fall as sales slow and unsold inventory remains high
item.description: November figures show prices down 1.5% from a year earlier, with more than 85,000 new homes awaiting buyers.

item.title: Tzvi Succot explains: This is why the Arabs demand the Education Committee
item.description: Five months after Tzvi Succot pledged to work to close an Arab high school in Jerusalem, police issued a closure order. The school, which operated without a license, was found to have prohibited Palestinian Authority teaching materials.
